stem:
A less-than cumulative frequency distribution for 80 students is:

Marks less than: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50
Cumulative freq: 5,  25, 55, 73, 80

What is the median mark?

per_option_rationale.rationale: n=80, n/2=40. Class frequencies: 5, 20, 30, 18, 7. The 40th value falls in class 20-30 (cf crosses 40 between 25 and 55). Median = 20 + ((40-25)/30)*10 = 20 + 5.00 = 25.00.
30 is the upper boundary of the median class; the student identifies the class but does not interpolate within it.
31.67 results from using cf_prev = 5 (only the first cumulative frequency) instead of 25: 20 + ((40-5)/30)*10 = 20 + 11.67 = 31.67.
27.5 arises from misreading the class frequency as 24 (instead of 30): 20 + ((40-25)/24)*10 = 20 + 6.25 = 26.25, or using (15/20)*10 = 7.5 with a different denominator.

explanation: Recover class frequencies from the ogive by taking differences: 5, 20, 30, 18, 7. Total n = 80, n/2 = 40. Cumulative frequencies: 5, 25, 55, 73, 80. The 40th observation falls in class 20-30 (cf goes from 25 to 55). Median = 20 + ((40-25)/30)*10 = 20 + 5.00 = 25.00.

explanation_sections.punchline: Recovering class frequencies from the ogive (as consecutive differences) is the essential setup step before interpolation.
explanation_sections.approach: Compute f = diff of consecutive cumulative frequencies: 20-30 class has f=55-25=30. Target n/2=40 lies here (cf_prev=25). Median = 20+((40-25)/30)*10 = 25.
explanation_sections.lesson: With less-than ogive data, cf_prev is the cumulative frequency at the lower boundary of the median class, read directly from the ogive.
explanation_sections.timing: 80 s. One extra step vs. a frequency table: recover f as differences. Using the first cumulative frequency as cf_prev is the classic trap.
